overview: The most fundamental division in all of biology, and the one that defines what counts as a 'microbe' versus a 'higher' organism.

aspects.label: Overview / Core Definition
aspects.valueA: Simple, single-celled organisms lacking a membrane-bound nucleus (bacteria and archaea).
aspects.valueB: Cells with a true, membrane-bound nucleus and membrane-bound organelles (fungi, protozoa, plants, animals).

aspects.label: Nucleus
aspects.valueA: No nuclear membrane; DNA is free in the cytoplasm, condensed into a nucleoid region.
aspects.valueB: True nucleus enclosed by a double membrane (nuclear envelope) containing the DNA.

aspects.label: Genome Structure
aspects.valueA: Single circular chromosome, often with additional small circular plasmids.
aspects.valueB: Multiple linear chromosomes organized with histone proteins, packaged in the nucleus.

aspects.label: Organelles
aspects.valueB: Membrane-bound organelles present (mitochondria, ER, Golgi); ribosomes are 80S (70S in mitochondria/chloroplasts).

aspects.label: Cell Division
aspects.valueB: Mitosis (and meiosis for gametes), involving a spindle apparatus.

overlay.memoryTrick: "Pro" = before the nucleus existed; "Eu" = true nucleus.
overlay.examHighYieldNote: 70S vs 80S ribosomes is exactly why certain antibiotics (targeting 70S) are selectively toxic to bacteria, not human cells.
